questions.question: List out the advantages & disadvantages of osmotic dehydration.
questions.solution_html:
• List out the advantages and disadvantages of osmotic dehydration/ [CO2]
  • Osmotic dehydration is a process where water is partially removed from fruits, vegetables, or
  • other food materials by immersing them in a hypertonic solution (such as sugar or salt solution).
  • It’s often used as a pre-treatment before drying, freezing, or other preservation methods.
  • Aspect Advantages Disadvantages
  • Product Quality Better color, flavor, and nutrients retained Possible solute taste alteration
  • Processing Gentle, low-temperature process Time-consuming
  • Energy Use Reduces drying energy High solute consumption
  • Shelf Life Lower water activity Nutrient leaching possible
  • Environmental Impact — Waste solution disposal issues

  • placing food items between two metal plates that are cooled to low temperatures. Immersion
  • freezing is a process in which ice forms within a supercooled liquid due to the presence of solid
  • particles that act as nucleation sites.

questions.question: Write a brief note on radappertization, radurization and radicidation.
questions.solution_html:
• Write a brief note on radappertization, radurization and radicidation? / [CO2]
  • Radappertization- A high-dose irradiation process (usually 30–40 kGy) used to achieve
  • commercial sterility of food.
  • Radurization: A pasteurization-level irradiation process (typically 0.75–10 kGy).
  • Radicidation : An irradiation process (around 2–8 kGy) aimed at destroying specific non-
  • spore-forming pathogenic microorganisms.

questions.question: Explain in detail on flash 18 process.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain in detail on flash 18 process? / [CO2] The
  • Flash 18 process is a continuous canning/sterilisation method in which the product is brought up
  • to sterilising temperature prior to filling, and the filling and sealing are done under pressure (≈ 18
  • psi above atmospheric) so that the product remains above its normal boiling point. This enables
  • sterilisation at higher temperature and shorter time, improving product quality
